1st rowSo. After reading my last review for this game and thinking on what the game is now,I see how good the game was when it first came out. This game is good. Solid gunplay,Nice stealth system,Keeps you on your toes when on the higher difficulties..But after awhile all of the dlcs coming out I started to think....Hmmm...This is getting a little pay to win-y. I moved on,Ignoring the thought until MORE DLC. And now...Now crimefest. Our 'Reward' for completing all of the challanges for crimefest...The black market update. The Copy and ♥♥♥♥ing paste of CSGO cases. Only 2 differances. The keys cost more and they give you stats. Now just read that second part again. 'They give you stats'. QUOTE FROM OVK ALMIR HIMSELF 'Microtransactions?I dread the thought of it!' Almir...Why must you lie to us?So yep,The game is fun,but really isn't so fun without DLC. And now the safes. The final bomb to the dozer..Or the final nail in the coffin..Whatever way you want to put it.
2nd rowRidiculously expensive to do anything with and the 'matched' duels are an utter joke. Wizzards don't seem to be capable of creating a playable online version of a game they've been making for 40 years.
3rd rowFifteen bucks for this? Are you out of your mind? Remember how the final boss of arcade fightan games would typically stomp the player super hard? Well strip down the mechanics of the fighting game to an oversimplifeid bare minimum and you get nidhogg. Maybe it's fun with friends but then again I wouldn't know--avoid this game unless you enjoy repetitive frustration.
4th rowKill enemies, wait until 10 waves of them respawn. Beat level. Beat up endlessly spawning enemies while attacking a boss from range until he is dead. Beat level. The levels are small, the combat repetetive and lackluster and it's really not worth anybodies time imo. Best thing about the game is the music which is fitting. But lack of any indication of taking damage or enemies taking damage really isn't fun, how much hp do the enemies have left, nobody knows... But hey it has trading cards.
5th rowThis game suffers from the same problems as indie developers, no foresight. The controls are non-customizable, with escape key closing the game window to ask you to leave. I'm reminded of playing nes simulators that lack sufficient controls. The movie for the first 10 minutes doesn't even sync right, with audio skips and finishing the intro to the game with a credit roll. I'd get my money back if I didn't get this game on steam. I'm so dissapointed with square enix, that I can't think straight. The controls are horrible, in a keyboard and mouse game you are forced to attempt to use camera controls with the keyboard, making micro-managing any battle nearly impossible. I gave up before even trying. While the mechanics seem appealing, there was no attempt made to port this to PC well. My rating overall is 3/10. 3/3 for graphics, 0/7 for playability.

79990Shadowrun Chronicles - Boston LockdownShadowrun Chronicles is essentially just a cyberpunk MMO someone slapped a Shadowrun sticker on. Truth be told I got it on sale for a mere $12 or so, and honestly I feel that's probably a fair price for what I did get. It's playable, I can see myself sinking some time into it just to get a turn-based squad combat fix. The game itself is extremely linear, you have no dialogue options which kills immersion. Playing a Summoning character, it baffles me that any time an NPC mentions something magic related my character responds like he's never summoned a spirit in his life. On top of that skill trees are treated less like Shadowrun build options and more like shoe-horned generic MMO. For example, my character is a summoner. I can summon a bear... that's my only option. In a true shadowrun game i'd be summoning all manner of spirits. I'd also not be a 'Summoner' I'd be either a mage or shaman who also summon spirits, not so much here. Basically everything that the Shadowrun Returns series has done absolutely correct the team behind Shadowrun Chronicles has decided to not do at all. My suggesiton? If you haven't purchased Shadowrun Returns, Dragonfall, or Hong Kong, use your money for those. They'll give you a more genuine Shadowrun experience. If you want a game where the developers clearly didn't know anything about the Shadowrun universe... go with this game and you too can own an Ares Predator pistol with an ammo capacity of 4...-1

79992FINAL FANTASY XIIIIt is the worst FF part I ever played. Open world starts in chapter 11 after 40 hours of gameplay. In those 40 hours you wander around in super linear surroundings with a movie clips literally every 3-5 minutes! The first 15 hours I thought that this was just the introduction. So you keep on playing. After 20ish hours you realize that this crap actually is the main story. By that time you dont want to give it away. Buying and Upgrading system is completely useless. Savepoints/shops are everywhere and you cannot buy anything useful anyway. There never comes a feeling up like: NIce I reached a city and maybe it has some new weapons for me. The time I reached the open world I felt more frustrated and overwhelmed because I expected the end to be more linear after 40 hours. Never buy this game. Don't let you get tricked by the graphics... This game is the perfect example that games are more than just graphics.-1

79995Dying LightPerhaps the definitive zombie-survival game to emerge during this zombie-themed game craze we've been experiencing lately (however I say this without having played DayZ - but I've played just about all the others on offer I think). From the creator's of Dead Island comes a very visually-polished game set in an open world zombie apocalypse. The game world consists of a city that is under quarantine due to an outbreak which (you guessed it) has been turning people in to zombies. Part of a military outfit and sent in alone to conduct missions on behalf of their interests; your character spends the game exploring the quarantined city and conducting missions on behalf of survivors and the various groups left in the city, in order to earn their trust and also a bit of scratch to upgrade your zombie-mashing gear. A perk levelling system exists which is quite deep and varied - keeping interacting with the world fresh, and the game is also heavily parkour-focused... making traversing the environment at high speed with a horde of zombies pursuing behind pretty fun. It does suffer from some of the same problems as the Assassin Creed series... sometimes you jump to ledges you never intended to, or it tries to intuit where you wanted to go incorrectly - however I found this still to be much less of an issue in this game than the AC series. A great feature is the multiplayer whereby you can progress through the storymode with mates, and when setting marker destinations on the map etc, the game prompts you with an option to create a competition out of reaching the destination first - there are a few prompts like this which are welcome and keep the momentum going. Overall, the price is steep but the game is good - definitely head and shoulders above the Dead Island entries. 4/51
79996A Date in the ParkA faux-90s point-and-click adventure game, A Date in the Park is a game about a dude who goes to a park in Portugal to meet up with a girl he met the previous evening. When he’s there, he ends up having to follow a few clues to finally meet up with her. This game is, frankly, pretty boring until you get to the end of it, at which point there’s a twist. Sadly, the twist is all there really is to this game; there’s nothing else really here. The twist is rather out of the blue, though there is some arguable foreshadowing for it; still, it is bizarre and frankly, it just wasn’t worth the time I spent on it to experience the twist.-1
